audit.whatIsWrong: First item is marked Garen in both layers while whys[5] on that same row reads 'First item is even'. The packet chart and the already-audited mirror both settle it as Skill: Garen / Garen / Garen / Garen / Skill / Skill / Cho'Gath.
audit.why: One row disagreed with its own explanation, with the packet, and with the mirror. Left alone, mirror-fix.js would overwrite it anyway.
audit.corrected: First item flipped to Skill in both layers, proposed with the whole chart group. Everything else already matches the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike describes Feast as crossing a 'true-damage threshold' with no cooldown given. Feast is 80/70/60 seconds and deals true damage outright; the first-item spike also gave no number for Vorpal Spikes.
audit.why: 80 seconds at rank 1 is the shape of the whole level-6 lane: he gets one Feast attempt per wave-and-a-half, and the rest of that time you are simply stronger.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] now carries Feast's 80s rank-1 cooldown and what its true damage means for itemisation; spikes[2] carries Vorpal Spikes at 8s at rank 1; mid carries Feral Scream at 11s at rank 1.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json R cd 80/70/60, E cd 8/7/6/5/4, W cd 11/10.5/10/9.5/9

audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. (a) Three fields call Vorpal Spikes his W — it is his E. His W is Feral Scream. (b) Feral Scream is never mentioned anywhere on the page, and it is a cone SILENCE. Against Garen that is the single most punishing ability in the kit: silenced, Judgment and Demacian Justice cannot be cast at all.
audit.why: The page tells the reader to trade in the wave to avoid poke from an ability that does not poke at range, while the ability that actually shuts down his entire kit goes unnamed.
audit.corrected: Vorpal Spikes correctly labelled (E) in spikes[2] and wants.foe[1]. Feral Scream named in mid and wants.you[1] with its 11s rank-1 cooldown and the instruction to bait it before committing, since its silence stops Judgment and Demacian Justice.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json W text and silence flag, E text

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page says that Feast's true damage makes stacked resistances the wrong answer, which the missing-interactions feed flagged for this matchup.
audit.why: A reader who buys Plated Steelcaps and Force of Nature to 'survive Cho' takes exactly the same Feast damage as one who buys health.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] now states it: armour and MR do nothing against Feast, so the answer is raw health and staying above its threshold.
sources: champ-data/_kits/chogath.json R trueDamage and percentHealth flags

edits.after: Feast is 80s at rank 1 and deals true damage — armour and MR do nothing against it, so the answer is raw health and staying above its threshold, not stacking resistances.

edits.before: Roughly even: your Judgment shreds his squishy early HP but his Vorpal Spikes (W) and Feast stacks start padding a health bar you can't burst through.
edits.after: Roughly even: Judgment shreds his early HP but Vorpal Spikes (E), 8s at rank 1, and Feast stacks start padding a bar you cannot burst through.

edits.before: Keep the boot on his throat through 5. Your damage still beats his through mid, but from 6 his R Feast is a true-damage execute - once you're low enough he can end a spin instantly, so trade in bursts, back off before the threshold, and don't greed the last tick.
edits.after: Keep the boot on his throat through 5, but respect Feral Scream: 11s at rank 1, a cone silence that stops Judgment and Demacian Justice dead. Bait it, then commit. From 6 Feast is true damage - trade in bursts and never greed the last tick.

edits.before: Trade in minion waves so his Vorpal Spikes W can't free-poke you

edits.after: Farm safely with Vorpal Spikes (E) and stack HP
